2026-08-27: root cause of the residual is that the reference hoists the load of the literal-pool constant 0x02000500 (`ldr r2, [pc, #48]`) and a dead `mov r3, lr` to the function's entry block, before the first `cmp`/branch, and keeps the OWNER_STATE_SIZE*owner product in r3 (`muls r3, r0`) so the branch-1 return is one `adds r0, r3, r2` reusing the pre-loaded r2 -- whereas our candidate computes the product into r0 (`muls r0, r3`) and reloads the same constant from the pool inline (`ldr r3, [pc, #40]`) right before the add, once per return site. Tried three source-level rewrites to influence this: (1) hoisting the 0x02000500 load into an explicit `u8 *base` local declared before the first `if`; (2) swapping the addition operand order to `OWNER_STATE_SIZE * owner + 0x02000500` (multiply-first, matching the reference's muls-then-add instruction order); (3) splitting the multiply out into its own `u32 offset` temporary assigned before the return. All three produced a byte-for-byte IDENTICAL compiled object to the original phrasing (confirmed via candidate-show, compile=fresh each time) -- GCC 2.95's front end canonicalizes all three source shapes to the same RTL before this scheduling/allocation decision is made, so none of them can reach it. This confirms the diff is a genuine backend scheduling/register-allocation artifact (most likely literal-pool load hoisting plus a local-alloc register choice, in the same family as the session's documented local-alloc.c tie-break dead end) rather than anything expressible as ordinary C source restructuring, and is not reachable without forcing scheduling or register assignment (prohibited by CONTRIBUTING.md). Restored the original source verbatim (byte-identical output to all three variants tried) and left status at measured-draft; this residual should be treated as a floor for this owner under the fixed toolchain unless a future session finds an as-yet-untried structural lever.
